1. Requires an account. Cannot test otherwise. 2. Privacy concerns. Users are forced to set up an account even to explore the app. That's a major concern and an invasive requirement. I do not want my personal, private information synced to a 3rd party server. Developers: Let us explore your app WITHOUT having to set up an account. Give us an option later of synching, locally or via iCloud if we chose to—and even to skip your servers! Respect our privacy — and let us try your app without an account; that is, to test the waters first! THANKS FOR YOUR RESPONSE, BUT YOU MISS THE KEY POINT! 1. Give us the ability to TEST your app without having to FIRST set up an account. We need to know if it's even a viable todo app before synching our data. 2. As to the privacy concerns, give users the OPTION to sync directly to their Mac if they would like to. Don't force 3rd party server syncing upon users! Better apps respect users' privacy concerns and give them options!

🚨 Small Business Buyer Beware: Asana's Rigid Billing Policy Is Outdated and Customer-Hostile. If you're a small business owner or solopreneur considering Asana for project management, think twice — especially before opting into an annual plan. I was just charged $265 for another year of a service I barely used and had actively tried to cancel last year. Because I no longer had access to the original email tied to my account, I couldn't cancel at the time, and after a full week of back-and-forth to verify my identity and finally gain access, Asana still refused to reverse the charge. This experience has been frustrating and disheartening. I've been a customer for three years, but their support team was completely inflexible — even in light of the fact that:. •The account was largely inactive,. •I had tried to cancel previously,. •And I reached out shortly after renewal. Many SaaS companies — especially those that understand the long-term value of goodwill — offer far more reasonable policies:. •Notion, a challenger brand in the productivity space, provides pro-rated or full refunds if contacted shortly after renewal. •Basecamp, a best-in-class tool built by people who genuinely understand small business needs, has a simple policy: "If you're not happy, we'll refund you—even after months.". Asana's approach, in contrast, feels outdated and overly focused on maximizing short-term revenue over user trust. That $265 may not mean much to a large enterprise, but for a small business? It's a significant hit — especially for software that was barely used. I've now canceled my subscription. If you value fairness, transparency, and support that actually supports you — consider other options.

Clunky messy ui. Sure it looks "clean" at first but it automatically adds markups that show every time you try to edit a word. So if you delete part of it you end up with bunch of asterisks to delete. That's not clean. Would prefer no markups at all. And having to pull up a secondary keyboard for every formatting task gets tiresome and kills work flow. Why not a long press menu for frequent formatting functions? And can't select more than one cell in tables. Honestly would rather go back to apple notes if wasn't so slow on my older device.
Great app at a great price. I love the Bear app. It's WAY better than Evernote and reasonably priced. Keep up the great work!
I'm using this nonstop now. I love this notes app is just what I needed! Though I'm giving this 4 stars because I really wish the lock notes feature would be free.

Sadly, voiceover support is lacking. I was really excited to try this app especially since so many people love it and because I'm looking for something that is simple that also supports wiki linking. unfortunately, as a VoiceOver user, I'm finding the app very difficult to use. Many of the buttons are not labeled and also voiceover has trouble tracking focus as I move around the app. As such, the app is currently not usable for me at least on iOS. I hope that the developers will consider adding more robust voiceover support in the future, I would definitely be a very happy user..

Exactly what I needed. I was looking for an Evernote alternative where I could use tags, and this is perfect. I both like to write and store recipes using tags for season, type, occasion etc. The support for nested tags is much appreciated, and their Pro plan is very reasonable. Not much is paywalled (it's just cloud features, themes, and search), so give it a try!

Almost. It's almost perfect, it won't render math or PDFs or anything, it was working, the update broke it. I love how it looks but the exporting and rendering are pretty fundamental and I feel like it should really be able to do more, like why not also have rich text as an option and if it's only markdown then it's a pretty high priority that it should do markdown literally flawlessly and it doesn't. Hope it gets fixed asap. If still recommend it but with warnings and if there were anything else better this app could easily lose to that. There are so few options for anything like this it's pretty mind blowing

Extremely suspect privacy policy. Expressly states data can be used for beta testing and worst of all the testing is done with what is quite arguably the least privacy conscious company of the 21st century: Microsoft. Not to be outdone, the rest of the policy is extremely vague but lends itself to the interpretation that absent written notice provided to either the developer or applicable authorities OR both (language isn't clear and would need to dive deeper), you have absolutely no it rly zero expectation of privacy here. In a market with 50 other competitors, this isn't the way to do business IMO. Massive wasted opportunity here

Just better than anything comparable. - It works. - It works consistently. - Great UI. - Smooth down to the smallest of interactions. - Fast. - Same great experience on every Apple device. No matter how many times I try other note taking apps, none of them come close to the simple, great experience of Bear.

Should need no introduction. Bear slaps. I've used it for like 8 years now. Super simple, just the right amount of complexity. Themes and styles are beautiful, including all the custom icons. Sync is always super fast and smooth. Exporting, tagging, formatting, all just work exactly how you'd want. Everything feels crisp and easy to use, especially and most importantly the note editor UI, which is truly perfect. Keep doing what you're doing dev team give somebody a raise

ipad rendering bugged for months now. when using bear on the ipad in windowed mode (not full screen), sometimes following a link within a note causes a bug with rendering where the bottom portion of the note is not rendered. you can sometimes fix it by restarting bear.

The very best! ♡. This app is reliable, easy to navigate, and stylish. I love using it every day! Please consider adding a feature for user-made themes in the future! And a feature to toggle a note's history + restore versions!

Bear is the Best! Hands down my favorite notes app I've ever used. It's getting more features all the time and has everything I need. Most aesthetically pleasing app, too. I love how it syncs across my iPad and MacBook, and the way it centers the content inside the window is an amazing but simple feature that not all other notes apps have. Well worth the money. My go-to for many years now. Small development team I believe, too, so I'm more than happy supporting this gem.

Great for saving info. Well, it was a great app, but the latest update just screwed up the copy and paste function. Used to be you could just copy and paste, then edit your data; now after you copy, it gives you a multiple choice for paste for which no selected options work, so they just rendered my favorite note taking app useless for copying data to edit.
Fantastic. Love it. It's a little glitchy sometimes but overall I love the design and feel

Almost Perfect Out of the Box. I would give it 5 stars if there was the ability to disable word wrap in code blocks and allow a sideways scroll. I do a lot of code snippets, but most lines are beyond the iPhone Pro Max screen width. Callouts could benefit from this as well. It would also be great if we could add or edit a CSS stylesheet file for the HTML export, or dare I ask for in-app style customizations beyond the prebuilt theme and the font face and size/spacing options (which are great by the way, thank you!). Finally, but not an issue of this app at all and not affecting its rating, would the developers PLEASE, PRETTY PLEASE make a Windows app, or at least a web app I could use on Windows? Then I would be a diehard forever customer.
Thank you for the safe space. This app feels safe, calm, useful, simple.

I want to love it so badly. Bear would be my perfect notes app, and I would gladly pay the subscription for it. However, the keyboard toolbar/text editor on iPhone is so bad, especially when compared with the default Apple notes. (Please just copy how Apple notes sets up their keyboard toolbar, it's so much better). If you want to format anything, it is such a headache and so incredibly slow because everything is hidden behind a formatting menu icon, which you have to press, select the formatting option you want, then change back to keyboard. This could very easily just be one button press like it is in Apple Notes. And considering how often I format notes, this time adds up quickly. Aesthetic at the cost of efficiency is useless. Also pls pls pls just copy the way Apple's todo lists work. I want to be able to drag around todo list items. Unfortunately, Bear is an app clearly designed to be used with a mouse and keyboard, not fingers and touchscreens. I think it is so beautiful, and I love the organizational structure with the tags and markdown. But this basic functionality that is missing is so core to a notes app that I will very sadly have to replace it with Apple notes. If they fix this, I'm buying the subscription and changing my review to 5 stars.
What I've been looking for. It's like it was made for me

All my work is gone. They updated the app and absolutely everything that I've kept there is gone and customer service has helped very very little. If ur gonna use the app at least keep your work backed up elsewhere

Indispensable. I do a ton of notetaking, and Bear is now my indispensable tool for doing so. The UX is great across iPhone, iPad, and Mac, syncing across devices just works with iCloud without any extra subscription, and the Markdown support is great for portability between systems like blogs.

Brilliant, lovely. So easy to use and intuitive. The aesthetics make it fun. I haven't found a better app for organizing all the notes, documents, links, and courses I collect and refer to to support my career-change coaching practice. The tagging system allows me to classify something by topic and also author or source. It's a beautiful personal library. And the customer service is extremely responsive.

Clean and Powerful. This app shines in the little details: it's crazy fast, compare it to Apple notes and you will see a night and day difference, especially for long notes. It has table of contents, which makes it easy to navigate long notes. The tag system is miles better than folders. You can manage your todos by following a thin line under each of your notes that shows the progress of your todos in the note. It supports latex! So you can write math formulas now. It has web access. It has a nice menu of themes. It shows you unmentioned backlinks: you can reference other notes that mention the title of your current note. You can lock notes with attachments. You can copy links to each note. You can export to multiple formats. You can draw (although here it's a bit basic) and have Bear detect words in your images. It gives you useful stats about your notes. And I could keep going. You would not tell half of these when you first open the app, and that's the point. Its power is modest. It enables you and gets out of the way so you can work. Their dev team is small and slow, but they deliver. Late sometimes, but they deliver. This app is a powerhouse.

Tried them all-came home to Bear. This app is so streamlined that it can be deceptive how brilliant it is. Bear works with your mind—without friction. Hashtags are one of five key power tools here. Use them to create a filing system, as well as to cross index any files you want. Bear seems simple, but it is in fact the most elegant writing tool out there. In its elegant simplicity exists ultimate creative power. As a fiction writer, with many large projects on my plate, I can tell you—as someone who has tried all the excellent writing apps out there—nothing comes close to Bear. It's exactly what it needs to be, leaves everything else in its wake, is created by people who design with pure intent, which is why it's literally pristine. Even if you doubt, master its incredibly simple tools, and build out a file system using the tags— they nest like breadcrumb trails...and there you go. You no longer have to choose a folder, or even a title. Just write, just flow, just go.

Perfect & Private. I've had this for years and love it. Just open and start writing, and the company does NOT extract or use any of your information, location, contacts, etc., which is a great sign of integrity, especially today.
almost good. if you could send notes to people like in evernote i would drop other note apps and go full bear. upgrade it and grab the money on the table bear

Voiceover users beware. I didn't even get to read the welcome notes before deleting this app. The side menu will not stop popping out, no matter what I do. The advice was to swipe right from the middle of the screen to avoid this but nothing worked. And if the welcome notes have titles, VO didn't read them. Just skip this one. Save yourself the headache.

Clean interface, intuitive function. I've tried pretty much every web clipping app out there in pursuit of the perfect system to store and organize my research. Bear comes pretty close! The UI is simple and uncluttered (super important to me as someone with difficulties navigating busy designs). The nesting note system keeps all my notes and clippings well organized and easily searchable. Unlike other Markdown-based apps I tried, there was no learning curve—use was completely intuitive, so I could get to work right away. I particularly like the note menu design with its ability to assign an icon to each category—again, as someone who has difficulty navigating dense text designs, the icons provide a helpful identifier to help me quickly navigate to my most-used categories.

Solid and beautiful text editor. I've used Bear for a few years now. I really enjoy the functionality, UI, and ease of formatting. I have the yearly subscription, so my notes sync across devices readily. I can also adjust font, spacing, and color themes easily. I'm not an advanced Markdown user, but I'm beginning to learn more features I've barely touched, like making your notes into your own pseudo-wiki (!). It's really nice.

Excellent for so many things. I've been using Bear Notes almost from the beginning. It was slow going at first and I hung in there as Bear moved closer and closer to 2.0 and I have to tell you after using nearly all of the options that are out there for note taking, journaling and more, there's no better. So if you're stuck with another note app, and want to see what else is out there, give Bear a try. You will not regret it. Excellent work developers, I look forward to being with you for years to come.

One of a kind! Beautiful, efficient, and versatile! This is a one-of-a-kind app that I've made an inextricable part of my daily flow. Truly, it's a masterpiece of elegance in software design. My only hope is the devs keep focus, as its versatility is going to encourage adamant recommendations for all kinds of added functionality and integration that could easily pull the app in a thousand different directions. I include myself among the masses. I wish the devs would add integration with the native iOS apps, especially the calendar and reminders.
Amo. Me gusta mucho,tiene muchas opciones de texto,puedes hacer de todo un poco,es buena para ipad y teléfonos,simplemente me encanta
不好用. 非常垃圾。辛苦写了几个小时的字全没了。不建议使用。
The best writing app. My only go to app for writing. I love it.

Lovely, but a few suggestions! I've been using Bear for years, long before Bear 2 released and it truly has come a long way! As a student, I don't use Bear for anything particularly professional. I'm just a person who enjoys keeping everything simple and organized. Bear is just that. It's easy to use yet has always been steps ahead of the iOS Notes app as far as features and UI go. I use other apps for structure and organization like Obsidian, but everything I do starts in Bear. If I need to write anything at all, I open Bear without feeling overwhelmed by assigning it a category immediately. I'm a Bear Pro user and I don't plan on letting go of Bear anytime soon so. here are a few tiny things I'd love to see in the future:. 1. There are a few instances where I like to be able to have a note throughout all of a tag's subtags and main page out of convenience. For example, if I have a note called "resources" with the tags #physics/GR and #physics, currently the tag will only appear in the GR subtag. 2. I wish the pencil icon next to external links could be disabled. 3. It would be nice if users could adjust the primary action that appears in the menu. For example, the current first attachment action is Take Photo and any other requires you to hold down the button. I personally use the Add Images option way more so it would be more convenient if users could decide what shortcut appears on top.

Just a few annoyances. Bear is one of my favorite note-taking apps. It's beautifully designed and incredibly intuitive to use. I just wish it had an archive option — sometimes I want to hide older notes without deleting them or cluttering my daily tags. Also, the Trash folder is always visible at the top of my tags, which can be a bit distracting. It would be nicer if it were hidden or moved to the bottom. Overall, it's an amazing app with just a couple of small things that could make it perfect.
Best Notes App. I've tried multiple brand name note taking apps and this is by far my favorite. Sleek, simple and has all the features I need.
App not syncing across devices - iOS 26 broke it. App not syncing across devices - seems to have broken with iOS 26. :(

Thank You Bear. Agree with most comments. Great UI, subpar UX. Need to consolidate between apps and shifted to Obsidian but that's for a personal decision across platforms and also for higher expressions of note taking that Bear doesn't have. One key plus is pasting images into the note, much easier than with Obsidian. But Bear has been a great mobile app.

very functional without extra junk. I replaced evernote with bear about 9 months ago and wish I had done it 2 years ago. Bear is super functional, I get pretty much everything I need. Get bear pro, it is completely worth it and the best deal of all the notes apps.

Used to like this more. There's been a UI revision in the last while that's made it super confusing to do things like add images to notes from my phone (go to BIU, open a keyboard, hold down on a camera icon, etc). It's not at all fluid.

My go-to writing app. I downloaded Bear back in 2016 and it's been my exclusive writing app since. The interface is intuitive yet non-intrusive, something very important to me. I can write without a bunch of buttons scattered across the screen and can pull them up easily when I do need them. The tag system is amazing and easy to work with and I love the small touches like changing tag icons! I write every day and it's thanks to Bear!

Great Note app for light formatting. I don't like the iOS Notes app much. I wanted a text editor with light formatting options, like WordPad in Windows. Bear is perfect for this. You can apply bold, italic, underline, strike-through or highlight to text, have bullet lists, numbered lists, H1, H2, H3. You can add footnotes. It's got pretty much everything I need. Hashtags make organization easy. These features are available with the free app, no subscription necessary.

Honest review. This app has nice features, but it doesn't beat Apple Notes, which is free. For specific needs, I already use Microsoft Word and Apple Pages. So I've got more than enough apps that cover everything Bear does, and more. The only edge is exporting to multiple formats, but copy and paste to Word or Pages does the job. Paying $30/year ($2.5/month) makes no sense with all the overlap. Subscriptions add up, and apps like Procreate or Inshot, for example, in their industry give much more for less money. I'd only consider paying for Bear with a one-time lifetime license price, or a much cheaper plan, where many more people wouldn't mind paying for, something like $10/year. For the features and design alone I would give 5 stars. But the pricing is overselling and overwhelming and the world full of subscriptions. If you decide to change your pricing plan, to something that makes more sense from a consumer standpoint, please let me know.

This is such a good application! I've been a Bear user for many years. It's very easy to use, making even complex sets of notes easy to create and manage. Bear puts the polish on notes like no other. The developers are actively adding new features, and updates are meaningful and useful. There are several very good notes apps out there, but Bear is excellent and elegant. Like your iPhone, Mac, or iPad, everything just works and works well.

Good, but files sometimes disappear. I have been using this note app to copy and organize my old recipes. It is easy enough to use, once one learns the special characters needed for anything outside of plain script. My problem is that notes occasionally are erased, through no keystroke I can find. If I try to correct a spelling, the note disappears, completely erased. It is not shown on the list, a search for key words finds nothing, and categories no longer show the note. Some of these are old family recipes, and if I have deleted the source copy, it is completely lost. This app is SO CLOSE to being exactly what I need, but how can I trust an app that saves "most" of the notes, but randomly drops others? If I need to keep an old copy, just to be safe, why would I need this one for a duplicate?

Almost perfect. Great note app does most things iOS notes can do and maybe more except make folders and sub folders to organize notes . And add audio files . If you could add these features I would say price is justified .

App is stutters and very buggy after mathjax update. This is a great app normally, but I hope the mathjax feature gets more polished soon, or please just revert this app back to previous version until the feature is more ready. As it is, the app is almost unusable for me.
Best App I have on my phone. I love this app!! It's so useful and a lot better than the regular notes app. Definitely recommend

Just wonderful. Like many other people, I have used practically every Notes app on the planet trying to find "the one". Bear is "the one". I think the biggest advantage Bear has is its broad feature set is grounded in focused simplicity. No app can be all things to all people and still be usable, so the developers have had to say "no" a lot. Making the vastly improved text editor is going to help Bear remain viable for a long time. I read in their Discourse community that they test the text editor with the entire Bible as a single note! The next big difference is going to be the upcoming web app.

Cute Idea. When I was looking for a notes app, the name and icon to this felt cute, so I checked it out. I like the simplicity and childlike feel to it. It has the features you would expect. A three columned layout, ability to create tags, ability to attach files, and plenty of text formatting options. One thing that I wasn't a fan of is how to create tags. You have to create a hashtag symbol in your note, rather than to just create a new tag in the folder list. Some tags may need to be repeated several times, and so I would rather create a new note from a folder that automatically assigns the tags. Aside from that, this is a cute little app, and I do recommend it.

New callouts are gamechanging... but. Callouts are exactly what Bear needed; they resolve the longstanding workaround of using quote blocks. I can comfortably say that with callouts there are no other notetaking apps that accomplish Bear's balance of utility and simplicity. That said I do have some constructive feedback:. 1. Spacing below callouts is awkward. Text/lists are either directly under the callout (as in touching the bottom edge) or have an additional line break that makes the following content seem unrelated. 2. A neutral callout background would be useful. The various colors are well-designed, but sometimes I find myself wanting the spatial separation without the added emphasis. 3. The option to use emojis as the icon could be useful. I appreciate the thoughtfulness behind the callout types, as it makes using them much less cumbersome, however having the option to replace the icon would make the callouts more versatile and personal. Thanks for great update!

Best Note Taking App. This might be my first review on the App Store. This is a fantastic app. I've used Onenote, Notion, Obsidian, and many others and keep coming back to bear for one reason. Simplicity. It can be as complex or as simple as you want, but the simplicity it creates for the user is just so good. It syncs with iCloud securely, and attachments are search with their super fast search. Highly recommend.

Sync Issues. I'm a big fan of this app, but over the last few years there's been sync issues, where my laptop and phone app disconnect and I'm not able to catch the disconnect/have to troubleshoot months later. The app also closes if I scroll too fast/far down the list.

DELETE NOTES RIGHT NOW! My original review trashed this app so badly—heck, I even called out the Apple editor!—that, looking back on it, I wonder what was wrong with me that day I reviewed it. Even without a subscription, there is so much you can do with this app. Has anyone ever complimented how great your Notes note looked? No, because Notes doesn't let you change its font, or let you add footnotes, or have half a dozen "heading" styles, or have anything else to make the note nice to look at. Bear has all I mentioned and more. As the current subtitle suggests, Bear has Markdown, the thing that lets you format with punctuation. You know—italics with asterisks, boldface with double asterisks, highlighting with double equal signs. If that sounds unappealing, there's an extra keyboard that lets you do all this without typing lots of random punctuation marks. This app has all that Notes has and so, so much more. I can only find two big issues: syncing and tags. Syncing between devices is a locked feature. Not every feature can be free, sure, but I'm not paying just to have the same notes in both places. It's not exactly a problem for me, but if you NEED to sync, it will be for you. The tag problem, however, is a problem every user has to deal with. Instead of folders, notes in Bear are organized solely by tags, created by doing #this. It's nice that notes that fit in multiple categories can have multiple tags, but this system is clunky, ugly,. and—forgive me, please—kind of stupid. Even after all the complaints other reviewers have made (not to mention my own first review), the developers absolutely refuse to change this. You've seen the responses! Despite its problems, Bear is the best notes app I know of. I deleted Notes a long time ago.

Awesome awesome awesome! This is a game changer, and I haven't even learned everything it can do! Honestly- all it seems to be missing is voice>text recording...and it wouldn't surprise me if there's a way to do it!
Bear is Awesome. Bear is just amazing, I love it so much.
Not digging the new. What has become of the ability to add existing photos from your library, or attachments to a note? I shouldn't have to reverse engineer this at all.

Good, But Poor Export. As an editor, it's good. It's not very logical during export, though. With any other note or document editor, if I increase the font in the editor, it exports with the larger font I set it to. Here? I exported a note as both a docx file and PDF, and it still exported with a small font size... even though I set it to 20+ font size. Also, images get cut off in PDF mode. At least have it export with one image per page via PDF... I don't find it worth paying for given that Google Docs can literally export in the same formats and it'll do it correctly.
Lifetime Purchase. Need lifetime purchase IMMEDIATELY
Notes disappeared. All of my notes that I've had for 4 years disappeared due to an "error" and I can't get them back. Switching to another notes app, what a disappointment.

Almost perfect. I've jumped around lately, trying other note apps, some with calendar integration, some with more features, but ultimately I come back to Bear. The tagging is so easy and clean, the sidebar isn't cluttered with things I don't use, and if I capture something quickly and don't tag it, it's already in the Untagged area awaiting processing. I have two tweaks that would make it 5-star. 1) let me create my own style, including highlight color, UI base color, and the rest. 2) allow for user created templates.

Greed is a sin. This is a 5 star app held back by one simple mistake: pricing. I would GLADLY pay this dev a one time double digit fee to flip the switch to use my own iCloud memory to sync notes between my devices, because this app is very intelligently put together. Unfortunately, they are attempting to charge a monthly fee for that service. You might argue that clicking buttons is very difficult and a monthly fee allows the dev to continue doing that full time. I would tell you that this app has received exactly one (very nice) visible improvement during the >2 years that I've used it.

Love it but please add folders. I absolutely love this application, but please add folders. Being able to have multiple different tags grouped together without having to have multiple tags on each note would be fantastic.
Pretty good. It's a good app but come on. Make it so when I check something odd, it automatically drops to the bottom. I dint want to switch back to notes but this drives me crazy.
great app for keeping track of any information. bear is not just good for taking notes, its also good for presentations and everyday use.

Nice UI, horrible UX. Overall, the app presents a visually appealing and thoughtfully designed aesthetic. However, from a functionality standpoint, the experience is significantly lacking. During my evaluation on an iPad, I found the process of attaching photos to a note to be particularly frustrating. The method for adding images from the photo library is far from intuitive—I had to resort to searching google for instructions, which reflects a serious shortcoming in the app's user experience. I previously used Bear regularly a couple of years ago and recently decided to revisit it. Unfortunately, it falls short when compared to Apple Notes, both in terms of usability and overall value. The interface feels unnecessarily complicated, and its lack of intuitiveness is a major barrier to productivity. While the app performs well for basic note-taking, any attempt to go beyond that requires external help, which should not be the case in a well-designed product. There is clear potential here, but the current user experience leaves much to be desired. I strongly recommend investing in more thorough UX research and usability testing to better align the interface with users' expectations and workflows.

Good & Smooth. Good, smooth app. Super helpful w/ all the extra quirks Apple does not have in notes. Only thing missing is the pinch to zoom like Pages has (for me). I wud give it 5 stars but I feel like customer service could be better. When they wrote back on inquiries there short & not very well explained. Short replies which makes more email response for at least the times I've reached out 😞. Other than that wish we had a sync button for manuel faster syncs.

No Cross Platform. I've been using this app on and off for years to journal but the lack of cross platform (pc or browser version with cloud sync) made me move to Obsidian. It's a shame because I'm choosing to pay double the price of Bear Pro for a subscription to Obsidian with enough space to accommodate my files. That money could be going to Bear if they had the capabilities. If cross-platform sync were implemented I would definitely consider coming back, but for now bye felicia

Simply the best note app. Bear is hands down the best note taking app. It works perfectly from the simplicity to the way notes are organized by tags, it's amazing. Now I just need them to make a "to-do" app!
Very functional. It seems hard to use at first but once you understand it it is a great app

Do not rely on sync. I had to reset my phone to factory condition, double checked that the sync was on and was backing my notes up to iCloud... Only to find out after resetting my phone that all of my notes were gone, and it synced to the sample notes on reinstall of the app. Absolutely worthless. I completely regret ever signing up for pro and spending my money on this.

Lightweight, blazing fast, perfect. It's like they took the simplicity, UI, speed, and system integration of apple notes and combined it with the QOL features of obsidian. Probably my favorite app on my iPhone along with a 29¢ finance app called Gem. Can't wait to get that web app too!
Nice. Really like the name of the app lol. 5/5 lessgo. Simply. Flat out. Lets advance.
Hang on to your notes. All of my notes were deleted upon update.

Sync is nightmare. I didn't use to use Bear on more than one device and I started recently and boy do I regret it. I've done all the expected fixes, update/delete & reinstall etc. But no matter what I do certain notes and a growing number of them at that are permanently stuck to the top of my list. Any sort option is the same and now there are so many stuck up there that navigating to the current note takes DIGGING!! Since the whole draw on this app is simplicity & ease of use I think my time with Bear is over. I have used it for a few years now but if I have to scroll through a long list of notes sorted by a mystery logic that murders the point is the app for me. Major bummer.

Quality App Uses Atypical Organization. Bear is a nicely designed app that uses an unusual tagging structure for file organization. I think it will work well for many users looking for an Apple Notes replacement that uses plain text however, certain design decisions make it unusable for me. Bear doesn't use a traditional hierarchy of directories for note organization but instead uses a tagging system that includes the option for nesting. Unfortunately, Bear doesn't offer the ability to filter on multiple tags at once, which is to say constructing a query as simple as "tag1 AND tag2 AND tag3" can't be handled in the UI without writing a string query. That's a dealbreaker for me. It's not exactly fair to judge Bear on this, but the general community opinion of the feature I'm describing seems to be negative, so I don't expect it to be added.

Not worth the coin. You have to pay to store to iCloud?! You have to pay to store to iCloud?! That's silly and greedy. I have been developing software for over 40 years. I can understand wanting to get paid for your work. But this limitation makes this software untestable for one's environment. Free apps do save to iCloud. It also doesn't allow you to edit the raw .md files, which free apps do as well. So where is the value add if you pay for it? None.
Awesome. Bear is an awesome note taking app. I've used it a few years and love it. The pricing is fair and the product is great.

Not "in-app" purchase. SUBSCRIPTION based! EDIT 04/16/25: Annual price raised to $29.99. Same complaints as before. Software is not a service and I will not RENT it from you. ——. Previous review:. I am sick and tired of all these apps that claim to be free with "in-app purchases" that you think will be a reasonable $3 or $5 price tag for something simple like the basic ability to sync your writing across two devices (something Google notes does for FREE) only to discover after you've installed it that it's SUBSCRIPTION based and will charge you $20 a year for something that should be a standard feature in a writing application! WARNING FOR TRANSFERRING NOTES. Let me start off by saying I love bear and have been using it for maybe half a decade now. So then here comes the issue: I recently got a new iPad and wanted to copy the notes from my old iPad onto the new one (I have the app on all my devices, but because I have the free version, I just copy and transfer whatever I need to). I hadn't had the chance to do that until today, so I had time to start new notes on this new device (including notes I take for my classes). I was under the assumption that restoring a backup would import all of the files that I saved a backup of on my old device. There was NO WARNING that my current notes would be deleted if I restored this data. I did not have a backup of the notes in my new device either. Again, this is a great app, but I can't forgive the lack of warning that caused me to lose all those incredibly important notes, even if in hindsight "restoring" data implies overwriting it. Even your average video game does this kind of warning. To the developers, please add clearer warnings and descriptions for what restoring a backup entails WITHIN THE APP, rather than just on your website. And to other app users, don't be stupid like me and accidentally overwrite all your local files!

There is one small feature I'd love to see, though, and while it may sound minor, it would make a big difference to my personal workflow: the ability to freely place blocks next to each other on a page without having to put them inside a separate card, page, or special container. For example, if I have three embedded videos, I'd love to simply drag them side by side and create a horizontal layout. Notion makes this very easy — you can just grab a block and pull it next to another one. In Craft, achieving something similar currently requires adding another layer of structure. It's a tiny detail compared with everything Craft already does so well, but for the way I work, it's probably the one thing Notion still has over Craft for me personally.

That said, the application of those formatting options is often clunky, unpredictable, or frustrating, much of which is derived from the whole "blocks" business, which feels like a weird and unnecessary thing when the app could simply treat text as any word processor does and let you edit elements discreetly instead of changes automatically being applied across whole areas of information just because they aren't separated by a paragraph break. Why is getting consistent paragraph breaks difficult, sometimes it double spaces, sometimes single and I can't edit that easily because efforts to delete the extra space instead only seem to delete the text formatting of the information after the cursor? The accumulation of these weird little behaviors adds up to a sense of overall frustration when it is not intuitively clear how to achieve the results I'm after. Most frustrating thing though, by far, is that unless I'm missing it, there is no undo button on the actual editing screen, so every time I make any mistake or the app doesn't behave as expected, I have to hit done, then another button to access the nested "undo" option and then two more buttons just to get back to where I was editing the note. Now imagine doing that 30 times in an hour. Just put undo/redo on the primary note editing screen and save us so much needless back-and-forth and this would be worth a full extra star immediately.

Feedback for Craft Team: Persistent "Zombie" Entry in Spotlight Settings. Subject: Technical Issue: Persistent "com.lukilabs.lukiapp" entry in macOS System Settings after uninstallation. I am writing to report a persistent technical issue regarding the uninstallation footprint of Craft on macOS (Mac Store version). [Issue Description] After uninstalling Craft, a "zombie" entry for com.lukilabs.lukiapp remains visible in System Settings > Siri & Spotlight > Search Results (App Results). Even after the app is physically deleted, the entry persists in the UI (sometimes with a generic icon). [Technical Investigation & Attempts] As a technical user, I have attempted the following high-level troubleshooting steps to no avail:. LaunchServices Reset: Ran lsregister -u on the specific path and attempted to kill the database. lsregister -dump previously showed the app indexed in .Trash, but even after clearing the Trash and unregistering, the UI remains. Preference Cleaning: Manually cleaned com.apple.Spotlight.plist by removing com.lukilabs.lukiapp from EnabledPreferenceRules and clearing queryViewOptions. Spotlight Reindexing: Executed mdutil -E / and deleted ~/Library/Metadata/CoreSpotlight. Cache Clearing: Purged com.apple.SystemSettings and cfprefsd caches. [Observation] It appears that because Craft is a Mac Catalyst app, it may be leaving behind stale metadata in the CoreSpotlight private store or the macOS SyncedPreferences (iCloud KVS) that isn't being properly flushed upon deletion. This results in a "ghost" toggle in the system settings that cannot be removed by standard user-level maintenance. [Request] Could you please investigate if the app can explicitly call index.deleteAllSearchableItems or a similar cleanup routine during its lifecycle, or provide a standalone "Deep Clean" script/command for users who encounter this "zombie" entry? Thank you for your attention to this detail. Craft is a great app, and I'd love to see a cleaner "exit" for the Mac version.
Calender Monthly View. I love love love this app BUT I really really really need the monthly view for the calendar😭😭😭 the vertical daily view is very difficult😭

Still a good app, but complex with bugs. it gets worse the longer you use it. Most Aesthetic Productivity App. This is by far the most cleanest and nicest looking app there is out there. Simpler, lighter Notion! It feels simpler and lighter than Notion, but excels in making beautiful Documents. Some notable features:. - Beautiful implementation of Daily-page idea. - Tasks are first class citizens here. Combined document-based tasks and standalone tasks beautifully in calendar timeline. - Document look-n-feel with backgrounds, banners, blocks... it's exceptionally good while maintaining simplicity of usages. Thanks for the awesome product! The only thing I could ask is - a lifetime pricing plan.

More appealing & better for mental health. I absolutely love Craft! It has been better for my mental health than the regular notes app and it is a lot more appealing due to its style, colors, and overall layout.

Incredible writing / notes app with terrible customer support. I have been using this app for all my writing this year and absolutely loving it, from the design to the performance of it. Great, but still some issues. I have been a user since the beginning. I Hate You Now. I praised your app, saying it was better than Noting Note, but after less than a month of use, it's showing "Block Limit Reached." It's incredibly low quality. Life Changing. Genuinely the best notes app I've ever used. It's the most intuitive, human, and simple app while leaving an ocean of additional features to explore while not feeling overwhelming. Hope they add more types of filters to collections. I really enjoy using Craft for notes and organizing my projects. It's intuitive, visually clean, and the AI features are super helpful. Exceptional. Truly one of the best note taking apps I've ever used. There are so many customization options and tools to use it the way that you want. At long last. For the past 4 years I've been slowly experimenting with "productivity" apps and tinkering with different digital systems to better organize my life and set up my daily flow. I've been building a "second brain". Most apps do too little. Several do too much. Apple notes is too flat and boring- I stopped taking and referencing notes when I switched to it. And Notion is far too cumbersome and technical- more time programming than utilizing. Craft does exactly what I need and does it very well. I'm a highly visual person and being able to easily give art direction to my notes transcend them from flat information to living texts. I'm eager to visit old notes and motivated to create new ones. When I put my thoughts into craft I feel like they continue to have a pulse.

Good but no undo button. I love this app. It's very easy and intuitive to use. It's better than Notion but my only problem is that you do not have a button to undo and that is very horrible in my opinion.

Beware - Craft LIMITS number of characters per note! Maximum of 20,000 characters per text. Maximum of 1,000 lines in a text. Maximum of 10,000 characters per line. Those are applicable to all types of subscriptions. ——————————————-. The above is the answer I received from support when I asked why I can't copy/paste a full transcript of a 2-hour lecture. (It would only paste part of it). I don't understand how this limitation helps Craft, but for me that's a deal breaker. Amazing how difficult it is to find an app suitable for studying (basic text formatting/highlighting, adding screenshots, inserting basic tables with basic formatting, column support). No fancy handwriting, no drawing, no databases, no commenting - just basic studying stuff that works without glitching. Why is that? (FYI, Notion worked for me for a while, but then suddenly it refused to work with magic keyboard. 🤦🏻‍♀️)

Really like this. Been using this app for a month or so now and this is the note app I have been looking for. Love the cal view and adding daily notes that tie all meetings that day together. This App is Awesome. The App is gorgeous. It is so multi-functional. I use it for note taking, research, script writing, document design, and web page design. Great app!

So Disappointed. Support really let me down when I needed them the most. Great app in many ways -that's why I've been a user for so long for ~ five years. But beware users or people contemplating using this app that it's very difficult to access your data if you ever need it or large quantities out of craft. I learned this when all of a sudden I couldn't add screenshots or photos or even move them between files. Several request, jumping through all the hoops for information that creating a ticket request, and never a response beyond the automated. I'm working on financials and taxes and desperately needed system to work. ChatGPT helped me figure out that maybe it was a space constraint and that using multiple spaces could make room for data. That's when I learned you can't move your data between spaces. You can't even export it without losing the formatting. I always knew you can't move more than one Photo out at a time, but I didn't realize the massive limitations equating to having your data locked up. After being down for about a half a week: the solution, you guessed it, pay more money for a different version with more space... Did I have an alternative? Nope. Like I said: great app in many ways but if you don't like being held hostage, be aware. You'll never be able to change apps without starting from scratch .... and God-forbid you actually need technical support. This one's kind of like learning the brother you love, is stealing from you. Too bad because up to this point this was one of the few services that I felt I could count on in my life & really our overall economy that is quickly evolving to quantity over quality ... which translates to where companies focus more on marketing than Support because this way they just replace the users they lose. I'm not going anywhere for the above reasons, so I hope Craft will fix these limitations because it's simply the right thing to do.

Improvements I'd like to see:. - It would be easier to find documents when you first open the app if you could see them in list view divided by Spaces and folders. Awesome! But could use some new AI models. Craft is an excellent notes, productivity, and AI writing app. However, like most apps, it has room for improvement, particularly regarding its AI models. The local AI features are impressive, but it would be beneficial to include more modern models, such as Qwen 3 with 0.6B parameters for local processing, or Llama 3.3. For cloud-based AI, while Craft already offers GPT-4o, this model feels somewhat dated now. Adding Claude 3.5 Haiku or Claude Opus 4 would be valuable upgrades. Alternatively, if sticking with OpenAI, o4-mini would provide a fast, intelligent, and cost-effective option. Beyond AI capabilities, Craft's interface is stylish and well-deserving of its App Store Design Award. If you want an alternative to Apple's built-in Notes app, or if you don't have a newer iPhone with Apple Intelligence but still want AI-powered note-taking, Craft is an excellent choice.
Please continue to focus on the consumers. I recently switched over Notion. I have been a long time Notion user but it has become too commercial and enterprisy. So far I like the Craft experience.

Not accessible... I was excited to give this app a try when I read the initial recommendation. It sounded fantastic, and being available across all my Apple devices, it seemed like a great option. Sadly, I was very disappointed to discover that, as a visually impaired VoiceOver screen reader user, the app is not well thought out for users such as myself. All the controls are read aloud as text boxes, and the main documents are completely inaccessible on Mac. I give the app 2 stars for concept, and it likely works great for sighted individuals, but I would say that there was little to no consideration of visually impaired or blind users when creating this app. If you rely on accessibility features such as VoiceOver, you'll need to look elsewhere at this point.

Perfect. Craft is stunning good and good looking. I use it for everything since Tasks were added. The designers are just plain smart. ADHD. This app is my go-to for everything! I've tried a bunch of note-taking apps, but this one is the best. It's super flexible and works great for my ADHD. The only thing I wish it had is support for fonts and the ability to write on my iPad.

The Best So Far. Craft gets rid of all of the noise from Notion while not becoming as barebones as Obsidian. It's a perfect balance of features—and it's done seamlessly. Syncing is immediate, and the app feels right at home on my Mac and my iPad.

Good developers build good apps. Great developers try, and listen to feedback when they get it wrong. My favorite thing about Craft isn't just that it was a good personal database app when I started using it. (even then, it felt like the more native, refined app I always wanted every time I tried Notion and found myself hating the very "web first" feel of it. It's that the developers have made wrong turns as they continue to improve it, and they've listened when users like me hated the changes. They found ways to keep giving me the experience that brought us here in the first place. I do hope to see less focus on AI moving forward. It's a frustrating experience that I want no part in. I just want speed, responsiveness, and a great document creating and linking experience. The Mac app feels like it's suffering more from bloat right now, and editing text is getting worse. But here on iPhone, I'm still loving it, and it pulls me more and more away from typical note taking apps and into Craft where I can link and organize everything to the level I like to. Finding a balance between making it immediate to create a new document, and making it possible to navigate the depths of a ton of organized information, is one of the hardest things I can think of for a notes app, but Craft does this really well. It's important, and it's been improving since I started using it. I hope Craft keeps focusing its effort on these kinds of refinements.

Long Live The Craft! This app has been a true game-changer relative to note taking for my graduate courses. Recently, I've taking to outlining chapters from my reading into succinct, bite-size notes. This is perfect for active recall sessions via the toggle button. Likewise, I'm also using it as a repository for information I'll need to keep long-term. It's been brilliant...not to mention how inviting the notes look with a little TLC applied. It makes going back into my notes less of a chore! That said, today Craft introduced Tables! That is another great and much need addition. Give Craft credit for hearing its consumers and making attempts to apply those suggestions offered. At a quick look, and limited use, Tables is welcomed in my note taking. I'll likely create a Table Template that I can use for specific notes that require graphed information. Finally, a word of suggestion. With Tables comes great responsibility. One area that will need to be incorporated, in my opinion, is the ability to Table & Database. Perhaps the only reason I continue to use Notion, is for the sheer strength of maninpulating data in its database function. If Craft offered that, I'd likely not need to use Notion at all, since I like the native capability and privacy of Craft. Collections is a great step in the direction -- not quite as functional as Notion. Great app! I'm super-impressed! I look forward to future updates and continuing to enjoy working in the Craft app. It's made my digital note-taking life so much more navigable! Kudos!!!!! PS. UPDATE MONTHS LATER : Craft continues to be impressive. Again, it's been a game-changer for my graduate courses. If you haven't looked at Craft, give it a shot. I'm giving it serious consideration, but I was really hoping for an icloud file based solution. I'm not sold on the solution as a whole for me, but it really is a great example of a top notch native utility app. I tip my hat to the devs for their hard work in bringing such a powerful app to spacial computing! Praise aside, do know it does cause performance issues with the AVP - I find it to be totally fine if I just leave it propped up next to my MVD and I'm not moving it around or running a bunch of other apps, but YMMV. Try before you buy. You're not out anything to test out the free version, or do a trial of the pro before you commit - and it is worth trying!

Gets Better and Better! Craft gets better and better with each version. The latest one brings so much to the table, with so many ways to style docs and make them unique and you're own for yourself or whether you're sharing them with publishable links (love that), to Collections to better manage data. The interface is beautiful and smooth, it makes it hard not to love using Craft. If I had to say one thing I don't like so much about it, and this could be two things, but they are in the same "user experience" category, which is I feel Craft sometimes makes you click more than you should have to, and should be more keyboard accessible for navigating the app. However, I have been told that this will be an area of focused improvement now that V3 is out. We'll see. Overall though, Craft is excellent with tons of really useful features, and their attention to detail with the interface and animations is fantastic!
Amazing Interface & Tons of Options. I've been a huge fan of Craft from my early days of using it. Now the app is even more feature packed. Gets better with each version.

I'm back. I left Craft after the substantial price increase and focus on business/teams. The app I fell in love with seemed to be going a different direction. However, with Craft 3, the company realigned their focus to where they started and offered some great sales to bring lifetime pricing back down. I am so happy to be back. Craft just works for my note taking style. It really helps managing large projects where everything can be organized out of one document, instead of jumping to multiple to find what I need. I really like the addition of task/todos, but it still needs some polishing to be great. Keep up the good work team! I'll be here for it.
A long waited must. using it for a week now. Seems like what most people expected from dropbox and elephant note.

Wow. I have used Evernote, Onenote, and Bear. They all fell short in various ways. Craft is easy to add to. It connects to my calendar, so it is almost the only place I need to spend my day. Its presentation and graphics capabilities allow me to create really fine documents. Sharing is a breeze, easier than Google docs, and more flexible. Tasks are still evolving, but they are already more than good. Preparing emails from Craft is easy, and I do that all the time. it is easy to share important stuff with my family. Any document I want to add can be added. Word, Pages, Excell, Powerpoint, Numbers, PDF, jpegs, videos, there are no limits! In addition to creating content, sharing content, it is a great place to store content for later retrieval! The Craft Team has done incredible work on multiple dimensions that no other app has approached.

Craft is intuitive and clean! Craft Notes has truly transformed the way I organize my thoughts and ideas with its incredibly intuitive design. The clean, minimalist interface allows for effortless navigation, ensuring that I can focus on creativity without the distraction of cluttered menus or complicated features. Every function is just a click away, streamlining my note-taking process and enhancing productivity. Whether I'm jotting down quick reminders or brainstorming complex projects, Craft Notes makes the experience both enjoyable and efficient, making it an indispensable tool in my daily routine.

Awesome app. If you're searching for an app to elevate your journaling, writing, planning, and organizing while appreciating sleek design and simplicity, look no further than Craft. It's one of my all-time favorites—a true game changer.
Craft keeps getting Better. I love how easy it is to use this tool and just the UI is clean, and simple.

100% Worth it. I have been using this app for several days now. I haven't had any issues. The built in ai feature has really been helpful into finding fulfilling ideas I could use. The app's really easy to use. I just love the style. I would highly recommend!

Great app, great team. These guys care a lot about their customers and about making a great product. Craft gives me superpowers — it's my outboard brain, making me smarter, more productive, and more thoughtful every day.

Productivity meets Design. Craft is an absolute masterpiece for note-taking and document organization. Its focus on clean, minimalist design is paired with incredible functionality—creating, formatting, and organizing notes has never been this intuitive. The ability to link pages and add rich media seamlessly elevates the experience, and the app syncs flawlessly across devices. Craft empowers creativity while remaining grounded in practicality. Whether you're a student, a professional, or a creative, Craft is the perfect companion for all your digital notes.

One-Stop Shop for Organizing Your Life!! I wanted to leave a review for this app 1) to ensure the Craft team's hard work and creativity gets recognized and 2) so others who love visually appealing and functional apps find this amazing tool! I have used multiple apps in the past to try and quilt together the features found in a calendar app, reminders/tasks app, journaling app etc. so I could "finally" get a holistic picture of what I have going on in my life. Not because I enjoyed using several apps - trust me I didn't - but because there just wasn't one that I could find to do everything I needed it to do. I honestly can't remember how I eventually found Craft, but I remember being suspicious at first that it could actually meet my needs. I downloaded it, then uninstalled it, then re-downloaded it again etc. :) but am happy I came back to the app and really dug into the functionality and features, because once I got used to it, the potential use cases started popping up all over and now I can confidently say that I use Craft for everything - my personal journal (I love the freedom to type an entry or insert a handwritten entry using the Sketch block feature) my planner for work (I use the daily notes feature to connect my work notes to a calendar date so I can take meeting notes and record ideas etc.), logs for hobbies, my meal planning log and recipe inventory, shopping lists, organizing my solopreneur business ideas, and for creative writing. Being able to setup a visual backdrop and create beautiful themes for projects really helps get me in the right mindset for writing and creating like no other tool has. It's part of my morning ritual now and I truly enjoy working within Craft. As a corporate employee, I can tell you there's value in taking the time to visually setup a creative space to help shift your mindset at the end of a work day (or before you even get started) towards creative work. I've tried writing in other apps but have always been uninspired by the minimalist, cold, and boring spaces in apps like Microsoft Word etc. Those apps always made me feel like I was still "working" when I wanted to shift into a more creative flow and relax into my writing or creative projects. One of the other things I love about Craft are the quality updates they push out. The last update added some really useful features like Collections (which are basically functional database tables), additional visual formatting options (totally for fun), and improved AI functionality. Since this is a paid app, you get the quality and features that come from a motivated team who's obviously very proud of their product. Reducing the number of apps I have to bounce in and out of on a daily basis has really simplified things for me. Almost forgot to mention, you can also access Craft on any platform - phone, laptop, iPad, webpage - so you always have your notes, planner, and journal with you no matter what device you're toting along. Love, love, love, this app!!! :)

Getting Better. Craft is a really good tool. Version 3 is a big improvement over previous versions. It feels like it is coming into its own now. For project management, I do wish they would add a calendar view that lets you filter events by assigned person or by project. Otherwise, this is very solid.

Decent enough. Pretty good app for notes and presentations. Some of the editing tools are in odd places, so designing as you go isn't very intuitive. The best note taking app. The craftsmanship the craft team brings is unseen from any other product. The app is so well designed such I finally successfully build my habit of note taking and jot down any reminders.

Amazing. Excellent platform to publish a doc
Love this App. I've really enjoyed using Craft over the years. The UI is incredible and the team is super responsive for support as well as adding new features!

10/10 reccommend. This app has helped me so, so much and it's SOOOO worth the subscription! But Craft not only has a beautiful, engaging interface but has all these cool features and they keep updating it and adding new things! It's probably the best purchase I've made as far as digital software is concerned. It makes me WANT to stay organized, it makes me want to use it! and I love how you can share docs so easily. Awesome app for medical field. I love the Task widget. I think the final step for this to be my top favorite app in one would be to have an apple watch compilation for tasks. Thank you. VR

Flashy but unsuitable for serious PKM. The UI is simple and aesthetically pleasing, unlike the bloated interfaces of other RDBs like Tana and Notion. They have ruined my love for this app. I loved the fact that my master list of TO DO could be transferred to next day with only the unchecked to follow. It was great help. I have no time to learn all the NEW complicated stuff. I thrive on simplicity without the frills and color etc. Not sure if I can continue using CRAFT When I had some things figured out to help me, they took them away.

Love this. Very very very useful I love the feature that lets you put groups of text into more groups while staying organized. Kinda wish it was more decorative, but it's okay I'm happy I found this app
For creative note takers. I've tried every note app available. No other app allows me to be as creative with my note taking as this app. Love the flexibility and possibilities! 🫶🏼

Fun and useful, a few quirks in the UI. I'm loving Craft. I wish it were easier to edit things on mobile. Craft is the essence of what Apple's Pages should embody. Craft is the office, documents, and notes handling solution for the rest of us. It's a fun and easy tool to create professional documents and more. I believe they've created an intuitive tool that meets our needs when filing, editing, redoing, searching, or converting documents. They achieve this through constant updates and improvements. The monthly payment is justified by these ongoing enhancements. Craft is currently the best document handling app in the Apple Store. I wonder how long it would take Apple to acquire this app.

So Far So Good. I won't lie, I downloaded like 5+ apps for each, note taking, calendar up dating, to do lists, journaling and more.... I looked at them all, played with them all. Deleted almost all. Craft was there, but there was so much to look at and see that I kept going to the others. Then I did it. I spent a few minutes in craft. Then a few more. And a few more after that. Deleted every single one of the other apps and have gone deep diving with craft. To do lists, perfect. Calendar tie in. Perfect. Journaling and more. Perfect. If you're looking for your one stop shop. Craft is it!

Craft Keeps Getting Better. I've absorbed everything from the recent v3 update and I can't believe how far this app has come. I switched to Craft back when it was just another one of the aesthetic writing apps, but it had the extra features of blocks, cards and subpages that I needed. Now there are so many capabilities in this app that it's up there with the Affinity apps, but for creating productivity. They keep adding more sophisticated features without losing the UI aesthetic. Everything looks good and I want to use this app for everything. Task management in Craft is about to replace one of my other apps. I used to keep a big list of tasks in my daily note and I had to keep moving the unfinished ones up to the current day. Now I can keep tasks in their context where they belong and just go over to the tasks tab to see them all and schedule them. My daily note has separate UI to show just today's tasks, which is way less overwhelming than a long list of tasks to pick from for today. I wasn't sure about the collection feature when it was first hyped, but it just clicked for me, and it's now the feature I'm excited to see more development on. Remember when Craft users were like "We need tags", and Craft was like "We got something coming", and we were like "What's taking so long? it's just a search construct with some UI". Now Craft has given us tags.. along with any other custom fields we want.. that we can apply to sub-pages within the context of a collection that exists as a table in some document that can be searched and organized and even related to other collections. It's got some limitations and flaws but it's very usable and I've already found several uses and I can't wait for more updates. I'm a software engineer and Craft gives me that tingly feeling when so much information is so well organized. Craft is one subscription I am not cancelling!

Best writing app I've ever had. I remember a few years ago feeling like I could never find a very well-designed writing app. It always felt like some aspects of the various apps were good, but they all had pain points that used to annoy me a lot. Then I found Craft and it felt like a perfect fit. I still try other writing apps from time to time out of curiosity, but none of them feel like this one does. The unique feature I like best is the way I can easily write or take notes in the app (or even in the web-app), and then easily share a link with others as a beautifully presented website. It's really clean, professional, and stylish, very unlike a typical "doc" that normally gets shared. This is a writing app that can connect me with other people in a way that makes me both look and feel good to them and myself as well. My 9-year old son uses it too! His favorite features are the amazing styling options, which he can tweak to his hearts content to make his writing look good. He says every time they add a new feature, he wonders, "Why didn't I think of that before?". Definitely give it a try and see if it works for you as well as it does for me! If you have tried it before, come back and have another look. They have recently added a lot of new features like task management and data collections, and I'm personally quite impressed.

Principal Design Director. from a design and functional flow perspective, quite possibly the greatest single piece of software I've ever used. This is where UX and design transcend into art and expression - without bulls*** or gimmick - the white board function is the only area of the app that isn't fully polished and it's still a lovely function piece. These folks know precisely how much is too much - tons and tons of functionally but it's all out of your way until you need it and when you do it's a joy to engage with. all the little details that actually add value - like the interface click sounds, subtle, precision - the segmented and context specific styling. - all of it, collectively bordering on magic. I've used/tried every PKM ever made - but I run my entire life on Craft

Great App!! I moved from a competitor and value this app more than most. It is not bloated like some competitors, and while it may not be all-purpose for some people, it works for me, so I'm not constantly switching back and forth. And, something I have never experienced is that one of the founders is active online and responds directly to questions and ideas. Wow! This one is worth checking out.

The one app you need to organize your life. I have used Evernote, Notion, Onenote and analog bullet journals but this is the one I am going to stick with. I get super nerdy when it comes to organizing my digital life so I've tried almost all of the PKM tools that are available, and while the extra features are awesome to have, Craft just works! It is blazingly fast and the mobile apps are just as speedy and full featured as the desktop app.

I Shouldn't be so quick to judge. But I can't help kind of hating this app. Maybe because I was so excited for it, the letdown feels so much greater. In my mind, the point of using craft instead of a much more capable tool like obsidian or Logseq is that it's beautiful. Naturally, the first thing I try to do is create some notes and then collect them on a document, styled as Craft's cards or pages. Guess what? You can't. Unless you had the foresight to create a note as a card, you're stuck with plain text links. Guess what happens when I try to style those plain links as cards? Instead of doing that, craft creates a new, empty page with my link as the title. The best part is that you can't even use the link anymore because tapping it only opens the keyboard. It feels as though everything is like this. When I actually try to DO something that leans into Craft's strengths. It just pushes back. I really wanted it to be my end all app, but it sure won't at this rate.

Wow, this tools has transformed by digital life... This is by far the best application to organize your whole life. It Is not just beautiful, but fast and easy to customize. Great job for the bunch of improvements in version 3.... Cannot wait to see what is next in your roadmap, great job!

At the time, I mainly switched due to Craft's ability to run offline while I was on a flight but the speed, responsiveness, and general level of polish of the experience kept me hooked. The ease of linking notes eventually led to creating a whole PKM system that has become indispensable. More recent features like the day notes, and tasks are just sweeting the pot further.

Craft is the Ultimate Beautifully Designed 2nd Brain. I discovered Craft via a YouTuber as I was diving into finding a way to keep track of all my projects, and I have a lot of them. I didn't want to use a project management software like Monday, Trello or Airtable - I wanted to think about this from a different way that is creative, intuitive and meticulously designed. When I saw it in action I quickly jumped in and instantly knew this was the right program for me. You have to understand how important it is to have a central hub for all your information, projects, tasks, sharing, seamless integration on IOS, presenting mode (that's new) and with the latest update V3, they have taken it to the absolute next level. Craft Review. A couple years ago, two of my friends were continuosly pushing me to join Craft. After some consideration, I gave into their encouragement and decided to check it out. I can honestly say that from about a week in I was hooked. Craft is for me an organizational tool and document creator that I cannot go a day without. As an assistant pastor, I use it for task lists, sermon preparation, blog posts, curriculum development, commentary, book reviews, colllege work, and so much more! If I could only recommend one app to everyone I know, Craft would be that app.

Phenomenal App. These guys at Craft seem to really want to design something great. I've been with them since right close to the beginning and they have been growing their app into something that is beautiful, fairly straightforward, and very, very useful. They did a Zoom call with me to get my feedback on what I believe should go into the app. Many of the things I discussed with Craft have been added since the call. It is becoming a place where I can organize my life. Since they recently added greater task functionality and calendar integration it has taken this app to the next level. The ability to use documents in combination with tasks and calendar integration allows me to design and engineer my work and life in ways I have never been able to do in any app. By the way, Craft, one thing that would be useful would be to have the option to see documents in a list view in both the desktop and iOS apps (this would more streamlined, would allow me to see and scan my documents more easily at a glance, and access them more quickly than larger form factor). Keep up the great work Craft!

Updates are amazing. Been using Craft for years. My initial obsession waned over time but the latest release has rejuvenated my love for using the app. It's just so well done and you can't go back to Notion or others because they just don't have the same feel.

A wonderful, beautiful, enjoyable document tool. Craft is much more than a note taking tool. I use and enjoy Craft every day to create documents that are both usable and reviewable by others. Being a User Experience Professional (UX) myself, I notice all the beautiful design details. It's clear to me that a UX pro has been involved in the development of Craft. I would recommend Craft to anyone who wants to take documents to the next level.

Beautiful but getting bloated. Beautiful app with great mobile interactions - I can do most things comfortably with my thumb. The AI features work well and feel worth the subscription price. But the navigation is just confusing. The home screen feels like a confusing mash-up of a Feed and Search that never clicked for me. The Organize screen would make more sense as home, but it's so visually busy that I often lose track of what I'm doing. I really dislike the document previews in the sidebar and wish I could edit them or turn them off altogether—I don't need to know what the document looks like just let me read what it's called. With Craft 3 adding Collections (a good addition but still no Tags) on top of a new focus on Tasks and Calendar, it feels like the app has lost sight of its core purpose as a document editor and is instead taking a new kitchen sink approach. Taken together, the new features have made the app more complicated than I bargained for.

You can depend on it with all your tasks. The general design of folders and documents eases the use of the app. The document section has a lot of tools for writing and editing your notes. The AI assistance is very helpful to do your stuff. This app is designed for multiple goals: making and editing notes, archiving your data, organizing, and planning your daily work.

A beautiful and practical platform. Craft is one of my all-time favorite platforms. The UI is gorgeous, but most importantly for me is Craft's practicality. Really Cool. I love AI and the way you can use it in this app is super helpful. I would for sure recommend this app to anyone who has trouble coming up with proper grammar or trouble finding the right words for things. With the chat gpt integrated into this it makes writing a lot easier.

Watch out! They'll hold your data hostage! I was a loyal Evernote user for years. I paid for premium, built my entire note system in it, and trusted the platform with a significant amount of personal and professional data. I eventually moved to Microsoft OneNote because it's more affordable and, frankly, has surpassed Evernote in both usability and value. Coming back now to retrieve my data has been a frustrating and disappointing experience. Features that used to be standard are now locked behind aggressive limitations. The web app refuses access due to notebook limits. Device restrictions prevent normal syncing. The overall experience feels intentionally designed to make it difficult to leave without paying again. Call it what you want, but from a user perspective it feels like my own data is being held behind artificial barriers. I understand companies need to monetize, but there's a difference between charging for features and creating friction around data access. This approach erodes trust and punishes long-time users who simply want to move on. I would strongly recommend that anyone considering Evernote think carefully about long-term data ownership and exit costs. Getting your information in is easy. Getting it out is another story.
